Sample.evidence_source: Overall, 17 patients took part in the focus groups, seven men and ten women, all undergoing treatment following suicide attempts, in the male and female acute psychiatric wards of the University Hospital of San Martino in Genoa, Italy (see Table 1).

Country.evidence_source: Overall, 17 patients took part in the focus groups, seven men and ten women, all undergoing treatment following suicide attempts, in the male and female acute psychiatric wards of the University Hospital of San Martino in Genoa, Italy (see Table 1).

Population.evidence_source: Overall, 17 patients took part in the focus groups, seven men and ten women, all undergoing treatment following suicide attempts, in the male and female acute psychiatric wards of the University Hospital of San Martino in Genoa, Italy (see Table 1).

Type.evidence_source: Among the different qualitative methods available we chose a focus group technique to carry out our research, in order to encourage group discussion in an empathic environment.

Area.evidence_source: (1) Causes of suicide attempt; (2) communication of the intent; (3) role of risk and (4) protective factors; (5) level of satisfaction with the quality of care; (6) role of health care professionals' empathy; (7) role of pharmacological and (8) non-pharmacological treatments; and (9) interventions to prevent further suicide attempts.
